items.text: From the Past

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Why won't you answer me?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I ... am still trying to understand the question.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: What? Are you so shocked I became a field nurse? Can't even spit out a proper sentence?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Apologies ... it must be shock. It has been so long since ... I ... heard news of you or your brother.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: My brother? His leg was torn up by a shell. They sent him to the rear hospital. He died right in front of me.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I ... I'm very sorry.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: No need to apologize. You're a soldier too.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Why did you come to the front?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I want to know how Walter died.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Searching for the cause of a man's death on the battlefield is meaningless.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: No one should die without a reason.
Her words leave Charon silent. For a long moment, he struggles to find the right words.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: How long you've spent here is not known to me, but it is clear you're a field nurse.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You ought to know that when faced with artillery, machine guns, and tanks, a man's life is brief and fragile. There is little worth in it.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Walter was struck by a shell—to know that much is a small mercy many are denied.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The words you spoke of Walter's death ... are merely a deflection. There was never meant to be an answer.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: That's not true. You know I'm not that kind of person.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You're the one who always brushed us off, dodged the truth, pretended nothing was wrong ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You're angry.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Why didn't you come home?
In such situations, even if there is no true answer, an answer must be found. Anything will do.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I ... no longer know how.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: We need you, Paul. Whether you're the man we knew or whoever it is you are now.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Why won't you come home? Why won't you see your mother and sister?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Why didn't you come to see us after we lost Walter?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Partita, it is not that there is no desire to give you an answer.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: He died right in front of you. So tell me ... what kind of artillery did it?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You have read the notebook. You already know—

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: No, I don't. There's only the date he died in there.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Shellfire. That's all.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I saw the ripped pages. Why did you tear out the rest of it?
The light fades from her eyes. Then, a short, bitter laugh escapes her.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I've had enough, Paul.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I watched my brother take his own life right in front of me.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Why?
Charon cannot fathom that a man who raised his sister would choose to take his own life.
Partita's eyes hold a bitter edge, yet perhaps it's herself she cannot forgive.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Once the wound got infected, it was like torture—he was just waiting for it to end.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I couldn't save him.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: All have done what they could. It wasn't your fault.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: A week after my brother died, you sent the letter saying Walter was gone. You mailed it to his house. I ran all the way there.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: It was raining that day. I slipped. When I grabbed the letter, I thought the blood on it was Walter's. But it was mine.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Partita.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Walter didn't die in front of me; I know that ... But, maybe that's why I ... I don't know ...

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I went on and on, foolishly, ridiculously, trying to find out how he died.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: And now, finally, I'm faced with the one person who knows what happened, and you just avoid me! It's my right to know, Paul!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Denial was not intended, nor was turning away.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You will find it, Partita, even in the wake of such loss. What you truly want to do, or ... what you were meant to do.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: But I can't! I just can't!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: In four days, this field hospital will be moved. The nurses will rotate.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You can return home. Walter and your brother would have wished for you to stay away from this conflict.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You were never meant to be part of this war.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Don't you see? We're all part of this war now! There's no escaping it!

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Before I ever stood here, my life was shattered to pieces. My past AND my future!
Charon lacks the strength to bear her pain. It is all he can do to endure the weight of it.
In the silence, her expression shifts into a form of helpless irony.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: None of this changes anything. We're just rearranging the rubble, that's all.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Go back to where they need you, Paul. I shouldn't be taking up so much of an officer's time.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I ... am sorry, Partita. Very sorry.
She simply turns and walks away.
Back in the trenches, Charon's work moves less smoothly than expected. It's as if a stone has slipped into the gears.
Even something as simple as checking for dog tags takes him longer than it used to.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Oi, Charon! What's with the slow hands today? Come on, let me show you how it's done.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Sorry. Thank you.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: That's the last of them. Guess that's our lot sorted for now.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Your graveyard's just a stone's throw from here, which means you don't have to rush off for once. Fancy a few rounds of Skat?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: No ... there is no need for cards.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Oh, come on, Charon! Sit down and play a few hands with us.

items.speaker: Soldier II
items.text: Save some time for the living for once, will you? Come on!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... I will watch for a while.

items.speaker: Soldier II
items.text: Still looking for whoever's in that photograph?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes. It will not be an easy task, but the search must go on.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Franz knows half the trench line by name. He'll ask around for you, but only if you beat him fair and square.

items.speaker: Soldier II
items.text: Yeah! Go on, all you have to do is win a hand against him! Isn't that right, Franz?

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Oh, give it a rest, you schemers! You're just after Charon's rations!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Rations?

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Well, you are out there day and night, scrounging around the battlefield like a proper rag-and-bone man!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The only purpose is to bury the dead with dignity.

items.speaker: Soldier II
items.text: Yeah, yeah, we know. But still, you've got to pick up all sorts of things, right? Cigarettes, bandages, parachute silk ...

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: That kind of stuff is more valuable to us than gold, Charon.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: True. I'd swap a medal for a dry bandage and a smoke any day.

items.speaker: Soldier II
items.text: Keep it down, Franz—best not let the major hear that.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Ahh, Eberhard couldn't care less about that sort of thing.
As they chatter, Charon methodically pulls cigarettes from his coat and stacks them on the shooting bench.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Take them. No need for games.
Franz lets out a long, dramatic whistle.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Ah, the perks of having Charon among the Frontgemeinschaft.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: There is hope that you will still help find who this photo belongs to.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Oh, no need for a trade, Charon. Of course we'll help you look.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: That's right, we were just pulling your leg so you'd play cards with us for once.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Ah. Understood.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: But the field hospital's getting moved in just four days. You know that, don't you?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes ... it is almost time you took your leave.
A rare smile flickers across Franz's face.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Yeah. I'll escort the evacuation team to the rear, then head back for my leave.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: But before that, I'll do my best to help you track down who the photo belongs to.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: And tomorrow, I'll find some time to help you bury the soldiers. No refusals, no thanks, alright?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Thank you.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: If I didn't know you better, I'd take that "thank you" as a challenge.
